title: Giraffes Can Do Simple Math, Scientists Find
summary:
Giraffes are the tallest land animals on Earth, famous for reaching high into the trees. Researchers from the University of Barcelona in Spain have found that giraffes can do simple math.

The team worked with four giraffes at the Barcelona Zoo. In an earlier study from 2023, the same giraffes were asked again and again to choose between two containers holding different amounts of carrots and zucchini. Each time, they picked the container with more carrots.

Since the giraffes clearly liked carrots, lead researcher Iker Loidi and his team used them again. They placed boxes on a table at the giraffes' eye level. The giraffes saw how many carrots were in two yellow boxes. Then they watched as the scientists added carrots from a green box to one of the yellow boxes. To get it right, a giraffe had to remember how many carrots were in each yellow box and pick the one with the most.

Two of the giraffes, named Nuru and Njano, picked the right box every time. The other two used shortcuts. Sometimes they picked whichever box the scientist's hand touched last. Other times they chose the box that had the most carrots at the start. The researchers think giraffes, like people, may have different ways of solving problems.

All the giraffes struggled when scientists took carrots away or moved them between boxes more than once. This suggests they may find it harder to track amounts that change several times. Still, the results show giraffes can keep track of small numbers.

The findings were published in the journal Scientific Reports on June 26, 2026. The scientists think basic math skills might help wild giraffes choose the best food or keep track of others in their group.
why_it_matters: The study suggests giraffes can keep track of small amounts, a skill that may help them choose food in the wild. It adds to research on how animals think and solve problems.

background_read: Scientists who study animal intelligence design careful tests to see what animals can notice, remember and figure out.
Being able to judge amounts can help animals, for example by choosing a spot with more food.
Giraffes live on African grasslands and eat leaves from tall trees, so finding good food sources matters for them.
Tests at zoos let researchers study animals up close using treats the animals enjoy, such as carrots.
